capabilities.name: abs
capabilities.doc: The magnitude of a number.

capabilities.name: min
capabilities.doc: The smaller of two numbers.

capabilities.name: max
capabilities.doc: The larger of two numbers.

capabilities.name: clamp
capabilities.signature: fn(x: float, low: float, high: float) -> float
capabilities.doc: A number pinned between two bounds.

capabilities.name: lerp
capabilities.signature: fn(a: float, b: float, t: float) -> float
capabilities.doc: A value between two others. `t` is not clamped.

capabilities.name: floor
capabilities.doc: The largest whole number no greater than this.

capabilities.name: ceil
capabilities.doc: The smallest whole number no less than this.

capabilities.name: round
capabilities.doc: The nearest whole number, halves rounding up.

capabilities.name: sqrt
capabilities.doc: The square root. Negative input yields a NaN.

capabilities.name: sin
capabilities.doc: The sine of an angle in radians.

capabilities.name: cos
capabilities.doc: The cosine of an angle in radians.

capabilities.name: atan2
capabilities.doc: The angle to a point, in radians.

capabilities.name: exp
capabilities.doc: Euler's number raised to this power.

capabilities.name: seconds
capabilities.doc: A duration in seconds. An identity, and the place a reader learns seconds are the base unit.

capabilities.name: milliseconds
capabilities.doc: A duration in milliseconds, for formatting. `250ms` is already 0.25 by the time this sees it.

capabilities.name: progress
capabilities.doc: How far through a duration something is, from 0 to 1. A zero total yields 1 rather than a NaN.

capabilities.name: agent
capabilities.doc: Resolve an agent by the id the consumer registered it under. Absent when there is none.

capabilities.name: wake
capabilities.signature: fn(agent: Agent, reason: String, priority: i32) -> void
capabilities.doc: Tell an agent something happened. Returns immediately; the agent acts at its next tick.

capabilities.name: consider
capabilities.doc: Ask an agent to think, at ordinary priority. Returns immediately.

capabilities.name: intentId
capabilities.doc: What the agent is doing now. Empty before its first tick.

capabilities.name: degraded
capabilities.doc: Whether the agent is over budget and running on its policy floor alone.

capabilities.name: reachable
capabilities.signature: fn(agent: Agent, x: float, y: float, z: float) -> bool
capabilities.doc: Whether a route exists from where this agent is to a point, without writing one.

capabilities.name: navigate
capabilities.signature: fn(agent: Agent, x: float, y: float, z: float) -> bool
capabilities.doc: Route this agent to a point. False when no route exists, and then it clears the old one.

capabilities.name: path
capabilities.doc: The route object this agent follows, for `drift/navigation` to read or steer along.

capabilities.name: deciding
capabilities.doc: Whether this peer decides this agent’s model intents. Elsewhere they arrive already taken.

capabilities.name: pose
capabilities.doc: A new pose at rest. This is where a bind pose comes from; take one and keep it.

capabilities.name: toRest
capabilities.doc: Return a pose to rest without allocating another, which is what a state machine does on re-entry.

capabilities.name: sample
capabilities.signature: fn(clip: Clip, at: f32, into: Pose) -> void
capabilities.doc: Sample a clip at a time. A channel no track mentions is left as it was, so a rotation-only clip preserves the rest of the pose.

capabilities.name: blend
capabilities.signature: fn(a: Pose, b: Pose, amount: f32, into: Pose) -> void
capabilities.doc: Blend two poses into a third, clamped at the ends. Safe when `into` is also `a` or `b`. It interpolates every channel, so `into` decides what an untouched joint blends from.

capabilities.name: blendSet
capabilities.signature: fn(tree: Blend, parameter: String, value: f32) -> void
capabilities.doc: Set one of a tree's parameters. A name no node in that tree declares is refused by name, because a typo that silently did nothing would present as an animation that will not respond. Both kinds of parameter are set this way: a blend weight, and a clock — the time a `clip` node named for its own sampling.

capabilities.name: blendAt
capabilities.signature: fn(tree: Blend, at: f32, into: Pose) -> void
capabilities.doc: Evaluate a whole tree into a pose. `at` is the clock for every node that did not name one of its own, so a tree of ordinary clips is sampled at one time and a node with a clock reads that parameter instead.

capabilities.name: reach
capabilities.signature: fn(skeleton: Skeleton, pose: Pose, root: u32, mid: u32, tip: u32, targetX: f32, targetY: f32, targetZ: f32, poleX: f32, poleY: f32, poleZ: f32) -> bool
capabilities.doc: Bend a two-bone chain so its tip reaches a target. Answers whether it was reachable; an unreachable target straightens the chain toward it rather than giving up.

capabilities.name: motion
capabilities.doc: A new root displacement, at zero. Take one and keep it; nothing here allocates per frame.

capabilities.name: rootMotion
capabilities.signature: fn(clip: Clip, joint: u32, from: f32, to: f32, into: Motion) -> void
capabilities.doc: How far the root travelled between two times, in its own frame at `from`. Loops are accumulated, so a clip that wraps between the two times still answers a step forward. Pair every call with `stripRoot` or the character moves twice.

capabilities.name: stripRoot
capabilities.signature: fn(clip: Clip, joint: u32, pose: Pose) -> void
capabilities.doc: Pin a sampled pose's root to the clip's value at time zero, so the displacement `rootMotion` handed you is not also in the pose. Every other joint is left as it was.

capabilities.name: motionX
capabilities.doc: The displacement along the root's own x axis at the earlier time.

capabilities.name: motionY
capabilities.doc: The displacement along the root's own y axis at the earlier time.

capabilities.name: motionZ
capabilities.doc: The displacement along the root's own z axis at the earlier time.

capabilities.name: motionTurnX
capabilities.doc: The x part of the rotation the root turned through, as a quaternion.

capabilities.name: motionTurnY
capabilities.doc: The y part of the rotation the root turned through, as a quaternion.

capabilities.name: motionTurnZ
capabilities.doc: The z part of the rotation the root turned through, as a quaternion.

capabilities.name: motionTurnW
capabilities.doc: The w part of the rotation the root turned through, as a quaternion. One means it did not turn.

capabilities.name: sound
capabilities.doc: Resolve a sound slot. Absent when nothing was registered or nothing decoded.

capabilities.name: play
capabilities.doc: Play a resolved sound through the mix.

capabilities.name: playPanned
capabilities.signature: fn(sound: Sound, gain: f32, pan: f32) -> void
capabilities.doc: Play a resolved sound at a stereo position, -1 left to 1 right.

capabilities.name: distanceGain
capabilities.doc: How loud something is at a distance, falling off to nothing at the radius.

capabilities.name: stereoPan
capabilities.signature: fn(dx: f32, dz: f32, yaw: f32) -> f32
capabilities.doc: Where something sits in the stereo field, relative to a listener facing yaw.

capabilities.name: tick
capabilities.doc: Advance the routine one tick. Answers 0 failed, 1 finished, 2 still going. Does nothing while paused.

capabilities.name: step
capabilities.doc: Advance one tick even while paused, which is what a step button is.

capabilities.name: restart
capabilities.doc: Forget where the routine had got to, so the next tick starts it from the top.

capabilities.name: setPaused
capabilities.doc: Hold this one agent while the world carries on.

capabilities.name: paused
capabilities.doc: Whether it is being held.

capabilities.name: status
capabilities.doc: What the last tick answered, without ticking again.

capabilities.name: doing
capabilities.doc: Whether the agent is currently inside a node of this name — the routine's own answer, not a copy of it.

capabilities.name: depth
capabilities.doc: How deep in the tree the last tick reached. For a debug readout.

capabilities.name: snap
capabilities.doc: Jump the camera to where it is heading, skipping the ease. What a scene cut needs.

capabilities.name: shotAge
capabilities.doc: Seconds since the current shot began. A read, so a deterministic function may ask.

capabilities.name: substance
capabilities.doc: A registered material by id, such as `oak`. Refuses in words naming what the world has.

capabilities.name: species
capabilities.doc: A registered species by id, such as `O2`. Refuses in words if the world has no such species.

capabilities.name: parcelCount
capabilities.doc: How many parcel handles have ever been issued, live or not.

capabilities.name: parcelAt
capabilities.doc: The handle at an index, for iteration. Check `alive` before reading it.

capabilities.name: alive
capabilities.doc: Whether a parcel still exists.

capabilities.name: substanceOf
capabilities.doc: What material a parcel is made of.

capabilities.name: temperature
capabilities.doc: K, averaged over the whole parcel.

capabilities.name: surfaceTemperature
capabilities.doc: K at the outermost shell — the one that decides whether it catches.

capabilities.name: coreTemperature
capabilities.doc: K at the innermost shell — the one that decides whether it is cooked.

capabilities.name: mass
capabilities.doc: How much of it there is, in kilograms. Falls as it burns.

capabilities.name: speciesMass
capabilities.signature: fn(chem: Chemistry, parcel: i32, species: Species) -> f32
capabilities.doc: kg of one species held anywhere in this parcel.

capabilities.name: moisture
capabilities.doc: kg of water per kg of dry matter — the dry basis, which is how moisture content is quoted. Under 0.25 will burn; over 0.35 will not.

capabilities.name: charFraction
capabilities.doc: Share of the parcel that is now carbon, 0 to 1.

capabilities.name: charDepth
capabilities.doc: Metres of char measured inward from the surface.

capabilities.name: wetness
capabilities.doc: kg of liquid water on the surface, per square metre of it.

capabilities.name: phase
capabilities.doc: 0 solid, 1 liquid, 2 gas, 3 mixed. Mixed is a real answer: wet wood is a solid and a liquid at once.

capabilities.name: burning
capabilities.doc: Whether a flame stands over it.

capabilities.name: smouldering
capabilities.doc: Whether it is glowing with no flame. A smoulder survives air a flame cannot, which is why smothering leaves embers.

capabilities.name: heatRelease
capabilities.doc: kW the reactions released last tick. A fire's size is its heat release rate, not its temperature. Negative while a surface is gasifying, which is correct.

capabilities.name: ignitionProgress
capabilities.doc: How close to catching, 0 to 1: the least satisfied of the five criteria. A readout — nothing branches on it.

capabilities.name: structuralIntegrity
capabilities.doc: How much is still load-bearing, 1 down to 0, as char eats the thickness. This package breaks nothing; it reports.

capabilities.name: massFlux
capabilities.doc: kg/(m²·s) of gas leaving the surface — the smoke.

capabilities.name: fuelFlux
capabilities.doc: The combustible share of that, which is what ignition is measured against.

capabilities.name: positionX
capabilities.doc: Where the consumer said this parcel is.

capabilities.name: positionY
capabilities.doc: Where the consumer said this parcel is.

capabilities.name: positionZ
capabilities.doc: Where the consumer said this parcel is.

capabilities.name: ambientTemperature
capabilities.signature: fn(chem: Chemistry, x: f32, y: f32, z: f32) -> f32
capabilities.doc: K of the air at a point.

capabilities.name: oxygenFraction
capabilities.signature: fn(chem: Chemistry, x: f32, y: f32, z: f32) -> f32
capabilities.doc: Volume fraction of oxygen. Air is 0.209; a flame stops near 0.14 and a smoulder near 0.05.

capabilities.name: humidity
capabilities.signature: fn(chem: Chemistry, x: f32, y: f32, z: f32) -> f32
capabilities.doc: Relative humidity, 0 to 1. Nothing dries in fog because the vapour pressure deficit is zero.

capabilities.name: pressure
capabilities.signature: fn(chem: Chemistry, x: f32, y: f32, z: f32) -> f32
capabilities.doc: Pascals. Rises where the air is heated and confined, which is what an explosion event reports on.

capabilities.name: concentration
capabilities.signature: fn(chem: Chemistry, species: Species, x: f32, y: f32, z: f32) -> f32
capabilities.doc: Parts per million by volume. The reading a game acts on — carbon monoxide is the one that kills.

capabilities.name: smokeDensity
capabilities.signature: fn(chem: Chemistry, x: f32, y: f32, z: f32) -> f32
capabilities.doc: Extinction coefficient, 1/m: what to attenuate a light along a ray by.

capabilities.name: visibility
capabilities.signature: fn(chem: Chemistry, x: f32, y: f32, z: f32) -> f32
capabilities.doc: How far you can see, metres. Clamped at ten kilometres.

capabilities.name: place
capabilities.signature: fn(chem: Chemistry, substance: Substance, kilograms: f32, area: f32, x: f32, y: f32, z: f32) -> i32
capabilities.doc: Put a new parcel in the world. `area` is the exposed surface in m², and it is required rather than defaulted: a characteristic depth is volume over area, so a parcel with no area has no depth.

capabilities.name: destroy
capabilities.doc: Remove a parcel. Its handle is never reused.

capabilities.name: move
capabilities.signature: fn(chem: Chemistry, parcel: i32, x: f32, y: f32, z: f32) -> void
capabilities.doc: Where it is. The consumer owns position; this package only reads it to work out what reaches it.

capabilities.name: addHeat
capabilities.signature: fn(chem: Chemistry, parcel: i32, joules: f32) -> void
capabilities.doc: Joules into the surface shell, which is what a flux from outside does.

capabilities.name: addHeatDeep
capabilities.signature: fn(chem: Chemistry, parcel: i32, shell: i32, joules: f32) -> void
capabilities.doc: Joules into a named shell. The difference from `addHeat` is a microwave and an oven.

capabilities.name: setTemperature
capabilities.signature: fn(chem: Chemistry, parcel: i32, kelvin: f32) -> void
capabilities.doc: Set every shell to a temperature. **For authoring and tests, not for a tick** — it discards whatever enthalpy was there rather than accounting for it.

capabilities.name: wet
capabilities.signature: fn(chem: Chemistry, parcel: i32, kilograms: f32) -> void
capabilities.doc: Pour water on it: real liquid water into the surface shell, where boiling will find it. Refuses, naming the material, where that material holds no water.

capabilities.name: dry
capabilities.signature: fn(chem: Chemistry, parcel: i32, kilograms: f32) -> void
capabilities.doc: Take surface water away: a cloth, a hot dry pan, or wind.

capabilities.name: ignite
capabilities.doc: Supply a pilot for one tick. **This does not start a fire** — it satisfies one of five criteria, so holding a match to wet wood does nothing.

capabilities.name: douse
capabilities.doc: Remove the pilot and the flame. Embers survive, which is the point of it.

capabilities.name: addSpecies
capabilities.signature: fn(chem: Chemistry, parcel: i32, species: Species, kilograms: f32) -> void
capabilities.doc: Salt the water, oil the pan, poison the well.

capabilities.name: mix
capabilities.signature: fn(chem: Chemistry, from: i32, into: i32) -> void
capabilities.doc: Pour one parcel into another; the first is consumed. Both must be the same material — a mixture of two is a third material, authored as one.

capabilities.name: release
capabilities.signature: fn(chem: Chemistry, species: Species, kilograms: f32, x: f32, y: f32, z: f32) -> void
capabilities.doc: A gas release into the air: a leak, a vent, an extinguisher.

capabilities.name: addAirHeat
capabilities.signature: fn(chem: Chemistry, joules: f32, x: f32, y: f32, z: f32) -> void
capabilities.doc: Joules into a cell of air, which is what a heater does and what a fire does to the room.

capabilities.name: eventCount
capabilities.doc: Events this tick. Cleared at the top of every one.

capabilities.name: eventKind
capabilities.doc: 0 ignited, 1 extinguished, 2 smoulderStart, 3 smoulderEnd, 4 consumed, 5 charred, 6 structuralFail, 7 frozen, 8 melted, 9 boiled, 10 condensed, 11 sublimed, 12 corroded, 13 calcined, 14 dissolved, 15 denatured, 16 browned, 17 caramelised, 18 fermented, 19 decayed, 20 exploded.

capabilities.name: eventParcel
capabilities.doc: Which parcel it happened to.

capabilities.name: eventSpecies
capabilities.doc: Which species, or -1 where the kind does not name one.

capabilities.name: eventValue
capabilities.doc: The kind's own quantity.

capabilities.name: create
capabilities.doc: A fresh entity with nothing on it. The handle is exact; do not put one in an `f32`.

capabilities.name: destroy
capabilities.doc: Remove an entity and every component it had. False when the handle was already stale.

capabilities.name: alive
capabilities.doc: Whether this handle still names a live entity. A handle to something destroyed is false, even after its slot is reused.

capabilities.name: has
capabilities.signature: fn(world: World, entity: Entity, component: String) -> bool
capabilities.doc: Whether an entity carries a component.

capabilities.name: attach
capabilities.signature: fn(world: World, entity: Entity, component: String) -> void
capabilities.doc: Give an entity a component, every field at the zero for its type. Set them with `write`.

capabilities.name: detach
capabilities.signature: fn(world: World, entity: Entity, component: String) -> bool
capabilities.doc: Take a component away. False when it did not have one.

capabilities.name: read
capabilities.signature: fn(world: World, entity: Entity, component: String, field: String) -> f64
capabilities.doc: One numeric field. Reading a field of a component an entity does not have is 0.

capabilities.name: write
capabilities.signature: fn(world: World, entity: Entity, component: String, field: String, value: f64) -> void
capabilities.doc: Set one numeric field.

capabilities.name: count
capabilities.doc: How many entities carry a component.

capabilities.name: at
capabilities.signature: fn(world: World, component: String, index: u32) -> Entity
capabilities.doc: The nth entity carrying a component. **The order is insertion modified by swap-removal**, so a walk that removes should count downwards — removing moves the last entity into a position already passed.

capabilities.name: findNearest
capabilities.signature: fn(world: World, component: String, fieldX: String, fieldY: String, fieldZ: String, x: float, y: float, z: float, radius: float) -> bool
capabilities.doc: Whether any entity carrying a component has position fields putting it within a radius, and the search `nearest` then reads. **A linear scan of that component's column, not an index** — the entity model keeps no spatial structure, so this costs one pass over everything carrying the component. Position is read from three fields you name, so nothing here knows what a transform is called.

capabilities.name: nearest
capabilities.doc: The entity the last `findNearest` on this world found. **Valid only until the next one**, and meaningless when that answered false — the same lifetime a raycast hit has.

capabilities.name: translateMode
capabilities.doc: Make this an arrow gizmo, which moves what it is on.

capabilities.name: rotateMode
capabilities.doc: Make this a ring gizmo, which turns what it is on.

capabilities.name: scaleMode
capabilities.doc: Make this a scale gizmo. Scale is always in the object’s own axes, whatever the space says, because a non-uniform scale along a world axis would shear it.

capabilities.name: gizmoMode
capabilities.doc: Which of the three the gizmo is: "translate", "rotate" or "scale".

capabilities.name: worldSpace
capabilities.doc: Point the handles along the world axes.

capabilities.name: localSpace
capabilities.doc: Point the handles along the object’s own axes.

capabilities.name: space
capabilities.doc: Which the handles are pointing along: "world" or "local".

capabilities.name: size
capabilities.doc: How big the gizmo is in metres. The host keeps this the same on screen as the camera moves.

capabilities.name: setSize
capabilities.doc: Set how big the gizmo is in metres. Non-positive draws nothing and picks nothing rather than failing.

capabilities.name: hovered
capabilities.doc: What the pointer is over, as a name: "none", or one of "translate.x", "translate.yz", "rotate.y", "scale.uniform" and their siblings.

capabilities.name: dragging
capabilities.doc: Whether a drag is running.

capabilities.name: dragAngle
capabilities.doc: How far a rotation drag has turned, in radians, signed and past a full turn if it went that far. Zero when the drag is not a rotation. This is what to snap or clamp; the rotation itself cannot tell a three-quarter turn from a quarter turn back.

capabilities.name: positionX
capabilities.doc: Where the thing being edited is, along x.

capabilities.name: positionY
capabilities.doc: The same, along y.

capabilities.name: positionZ
capabilities.doc: The same, along z.

capabilities.name: setPosition
capabilities.signature: fn(gizmo: Gizmo, x: f32, y: f32, z: f32) -> void
capabilities.doc: Put the gizmo, and the transform it is editing, somewhere. A drag that is running is not interrupted, so do this between drags.

capabilities.name: scaleX
capabilities.doc: How much the thing being edited is scaled, along x.

capabilities.name: scaleY
capabilities.doc: The same, along y.

capabilities.name: scaleZ
capabilities.doc: The same, along z.

capabilities.name: rotationX
capabilities.doc: The orientation being edited, as a quaternion: x.

capabilities.name: rotationY
capabilities.doc: The same: y.

capabilities.name: rotationZ
capabilities.doc: The same: z.

capabilities.name: rotationW
capabilities.doc: The same: w. Identity is (0, 0, 0, 1).

capabilities.name: mode
capabilities.doc: What the editor is doing: "edit", "play" or "paused".

capabilities.name: playing
capabilities.doc: Whether the world is advancing. False while paused and while editing.

capabilities.name: play
capabilities.doc: Start playing, taking a snapshot of the world first so `stop` can put it back. Resuming from paused does not re-snapshot. False when no world is bound to snapshot.

capabilities.name: pause
capabilities.doc: Hold the world where it is. The frame keeps drawing.

capabilities.name: step
capabilities.doc: Advance exactly one fixed tick, then hold. Does nothing while editing, where there is nothing to step.

capabilities.name: stop
capabilities.doc: Leave play and put the world back as it was. Every entity handle changes, so a selection is re-found by its place in the snapshot and one that play created is dropped. False when there was nothing to put back.

capabilities.name: rowCount
capabilities.doc: How many rows the tree showed at its last rebuild.

capabilities.name: rebuildTree
capabilities.doc: Walk a node and everything under it into rows, honouring which branches are collapsed.

capabilities.name: rowName
capabilities.doc: What the node on a row is called, or "" for a row that does not exist.

capabilities.name: rowDepth
capabilities.doc: How deep a row sits, with the root at zero. Minus one for a row that does not exist.

capabilities.name: rowExpanded
capabilities.doc: Whether a row is showing its children. Meaningless for a row with none.

capabilities.name: toggleRow
capabilities.doc: Open a closed row or close an open one. Call `rebuildTree` afterwards to see it.

capabilities.name: selectRow
capabilities.doc: Select the node on a row, which points the gizmo at it. A row that does not exist selects nothing.

capabilities.name: selectedRow
capabilities.doc: Which row is selected, or minus one.

capabilities.name: fieldCount
capabilities.doc: How many fields the inspector is showing.

capabilities.name: fieldLabel
capabilities.doc: A field’s name as it was declared, or "" for a field that does not exist.

capabilities.name: fieldGroup
capabilities.doc: What a field belongs to: a component’s name, or "transform" for a node.

capabilities.name: fieldKind
capabilities.doc: How to show a field: "number", "integer", "boolean", "text", "entity" or "enum". Taken from the declared type, because a read cannot tell them apart.

capabilities.name: fieldNumber
capabilities.doc: A field’s value as a number. Zero for a field that is not one, and for one that does not exist.

capabilities.name: setFieldNumber
capabilities.signature: fn(editor: Editor, field: i32, value: f32) -> bool
capabilities.doc: Write a number into a field. False where the field does not exist or will not take one.

capabilities.name: self
capabilities.doc: Which participant this peer is. Fixed for the life of the session, which is why a deterministic system may read it.

capabilities.name: authority
capabilities.doc: Whether this peer’s world is the authoritative one. Fixed when the session is created.

capabilities.name: participants
capabilities.doc: How many participants the session holds. Nondeterministic because somebody may join or leave between two runs of the same recording.

capabilities.name: confirmed
capabilities.doc: The highest tick every participant’s input has arrived for, or -1. Moves with packet timing, so a deterministic system may not branch on it.

capabilities.name: halted
capabilities.doc: Whether the session has stopped, because an input arrived too late to apply or two peers computed different worlds.

capabilities.name: haltReason
capabilities.doc: Why it halted, as a sentence, or an empty string. Names the tick a divergence began at.

capabilities.name: slots
capabilities.doc: How many replicated scalars each participant has. A consumer sizes this when the session is made.

capabilities.name: replicated
capabilities.signature: fn(session: Session, participant: i32, slot: i32) -> f32
capabilities.doc: Read a participant’s published scalar. An index out of range answers zero rather than failing, because a frame loop has nothing to do with a refusal.

capabilities.name: replicate
capabilities.signature: fn(session: Session, slot: i32, value: f32) -> void
capabilities.doc: Publish a value in one of this peer’s slots. Not callable from a deterministic system: a replay re-runs one and a send is not idempotent.

capabilities.name: tick
capabilities.doc: The last tick that was stepped, or -1 before the first.

capabilities.name: isReplaying
capabilities.doc: Whether this tick is being re-run to correct a mispredicted one. Anything that should not happen twice — a sound, a particle, a message — asks this first.

capabilities.name: depth
capabilities.doc: How many ticks back a rewind can reach. Eight at 60 Hz is 133 milliseconds of correction.

capabilities.name: earliest
capabilities.doc: The oldest tick still retained, or -1. An input older than this cannot be applied and the session cannot be made correct.

capabilities.name: replays
capabilities.doc: How many rewinds have happened. A session correcting constantly has a link problem.

capabilities.name: replayedTicks
capabilities.doc: How many ticks those rewinds re-ran in total. Divided by `replays`, the average depth of a correction.

capabilities.name: query
capabilities.signature: fn(world: World, a: String, b: String, c: String, d: String) -> Cursor
capabilities.doc: Open a walk over everything carrying these components. The cursor is borrowed from the world’s pool; ending the walk gives it back.

capabilities.name: without
capabilities.doc: Narrow an open walk to entities that do **not** carry a component.

capabilities.name: next
capabilities.doc: The next entity, or a **negative** number when the walk is done — which also gives the cursor back. Negative rather than zero, because zero is a legal handle.

capabilities.name: view
capabilities.signature: fn(world: World, component: String, forWriting: bool) -> View
capabilities.doc: A component’s live columns. `forWriting` decides which of a system’s declarations is checked — a loop that only reads takes a readable view, and asking for more than the system declared is refused.

capabilities.name: push
capabilities.signature: fn(queue: Queue, id: String, priority: f32, holdFor: f32) -> void
capabilities.doc: Queue a message by identity. A repeat of the same id inside the dedupe window is dropped.

capabilities.name: current
capabilities.doc: The id of the message showing now, if any. The queue carries identity and priority; the words are the consumer's.

capabilities.name: clear
capabilities.doc: Drop everything queued.

capabilities.name: down
capabilities.doc: Whether an action is held.

capabilities.name: pressed
capabilities.doc: Whether an action went down this frame.

capabilities.name: axisX
capabilities.doc: A directional action's horizontal component, shortened to the rim with the vertical one so a keyboard diagonal is not faster than a straight line. For two independent controls such as throttle and steering, read rawAxisX instead.

capabilities.name: axisY
capabilities.doc: A directional action's vertical component, shortened to the rim with the horizontal one. For two independent controls, read rawAxisY instead.

capabilities.name: rawAxisX
capabilities.doc: An action's horizontal axis on its own, not shortened against the vertical one. This is what a throttle or a steering input wants: holding two keys gives a full 1 on each.

capabilities.name: rawAxisY
capabilities.doc: An action's vertical axis on its own, not shortened against the horizontal one.

capabilities.name: canRumble
capabilities.doc: Whether the pad these actions read has motors this browser can drive. Grey the control out when it is false; most pads on most browsers cannot.

capabilities.name: rumble
capabilities.signature: fn(actions: Actions, durationMs: f32, strong: f32, weak: f32) -> bool
capabilities.doc: Rumble for a duration in milliseconds, at two magnitudes in [0, 1]: `strong` is the low-frequency motor and `weak` the high-frequency one. Answers whether the platform took it; false is a real answer, not an error.

capabilities.name: stopRumble
capabilities.doc: Stop whatever that pad is playing. Answers whether the platform took it.

capabilities.name: nearest
capabilities.signature: fn(graph: NavGraph, x: float, y: float, z: float) -> i32
capabilities.doc: The node nearest a place, or -1 where the graph has none. How an agent gets onto the network.

capabilities.name: nearestWithin
capabilities.signature: fn(graph: NavGraph, x: float, y: float, z: float, maxDistance: float) -> i32
capabilities.doc: The nearest node within a distance, or -1. Use it so an agent that has walked off the network is not snapped to the far side of the map.

capabilities.name: route
capabilities.signature: fn(path: NavPath, graph: NavGraph, fromX: float, fromY: float, fromZ: float, toX: float, toY: float, toZ: float) -> bool
capabilities.doc: Path from one place to another, storing the route. False where there is no way through, which is an answer and not a failure.

capabilities.name: routeBetween
capabilities.signature: fn(path: NavPath, graph: NavGraph, from: i32, to: i32) -> bool
capabilities.doc: The same, between two nodes you already have. For a consumer with their own spatial index.

capabilities.name: path
capabilities.doc: The route this agent is following, kept by the host between steps. Empty until something routes it, and empty again if the agent's handle is reused.

capabilities.name: clear
capabilities.doc: Forget the route. The walker is then arrived, wherever it is.

capabilities.name: following
capabilities.doc: Whether there is a route to follow.

capabilities.name: steerX
capabilities.signature: fn(path: NavPath, x: float, y: float, z: float) -> float
capabilities.doc: Where a walker at this place should aim, along x. A point ahead on the path rather than the next node, so corners are cut smoothly instead of snapped at.

capabilities.name: steerY
capabilities.signature: fn(path: NavPath, x: float, y: float, z: float) -> float
capabilities.doc: The same aim point, along y.

capabilities.name: steerZ
capabilities.signature: fn(path: NavPath, x: float, y: float, z: float) -> float
capabilities.doc: The same aim point, along z.

capabilities.name: remaining
capabilities.signature: fn(path: NavPath, x: float, y: float, z: float) -> float
capabilities.doc: How far is left, following the path rather than as the crow flies.

capabilities.name: arrived
capabilities.signature: fn(path: NavPath, x: float, y: float, z: float) -> bool
capabilities.doc: Whether the walker is there. True with no route at all, so one check covers both.

capabilities.name: read
capabilities.doc: What is stored under a key. Absent when nothing is, which is ordinary rather than exceptional.

capabilities.name: write
capabilities.signature: fn(store: Store, key: String, value: String) -> void
capabilities.doc: Store a value under a key.

capabilities.name: remove
capabilities.doc: Forget a key.

capabilities.name: saveStatus
capabilities.doc: Whether writes have landed: `idle`, `pending`, `saving` or `failed`. A store that writes synchronously is always `idle`, which is the true answer rather than a stub.

capabilities.name: pendingSaves
capabilities.doc: How many keys are waiting to reach the backend. Zero for a store that writes synchronously.

capabilities.name: colliderCount
capabilities.doc: How many colliders a set holds.

capabilities.name: colliderCapacity
capabilities.doc: How many slots the set has allocated, live or not. Equal to `colliderCount` until a group is removed; after that the live colliders are sparse within it.

capabilities.name: colliderBytes
capabilities.doc: What the set costs in memory, in bytes. The slots and shapes are exact; the spatial index includes an estimate of per-object overhead a JavaScript engine does not expose.

capabilities.name: beginColliderGroup
capabilities.doc: Open a group. Add boxes with `addColliderBox`, then `endColliderGroup` to put them in and get the handle back.

capabilities.name: addColliderBox
capabilities.signature: fn(colliders: Colliders, cx: f32, cy: f32, cz: f32, hx: f32, hy: f32, hz: f32) -> void
capabilities.doc: A box in the open group, by centre and half-extents — the same numbers a mesh builder takes, so nothing is authored twice. Nothing is queryable until `endColliderGroup`.

capabilities.name: endColliderGroup
capabilities.doc: Put the open group into the set and return the handle that drops it again. Keep the handle: it is the only way to remove those colliders.

capabilities.name: removeColliderGroup
capabilities.doc: Drop a group and everything in it. Refuses a handle the set does not hold, and refuses the colliders the set was constructed with — a set meant to stream is constructed empty.

capabilities.name: anyWithin
capabilities.signature: fn(colliders: Colliders, x: f32, y: f32, z: f32, radius: f32) -> bool
capabilities.doc: Whether any collider overlaps the *box* around a sphere. The cheapest answer there is, and it over-reports a collider that only reaches the box corners. `nearestWithin` measures the sphere.

capabilities.name: nearestWithin
capabilities.signature: fn(colliders: Colliders, x: f32, y: f32, z: f32, radius: f32) -> bool
capabilities.doc: Find the closest collider within a radius and record it. Read the result with the `near` functions. Valid until the next `nearestWithin` on this set.

capabilities.name: nearCollider
capabilities.doc: The collider the last `nearestWithin` on this set found, or −1.

capabilities.name: nearX
capabilities.doc: The closest point on that collider’s bounds, along x — the point on the wall rather than the wall’s centre.

capabilities.name: nearY
capabilities.doc: The closest point on that collider’s bounds, along y.

capabilities.name: nearZ
capabilities.doc: The closest point on that collider’s bounds, along z.

capabilities.name: nearDistance
capabilities.doc: How far that collider’s bounds are, in metres. Zero when the query point is inside them.

capabilities.name: bodyCount
capabilities.doc: How many bodies the world holds.

capabilities.name: bodyX
capabilities.doc: A body's world position along x.

capabilities.name: bodyY
capabilities.doc: A body's world position along y.

capabilities.name: bodyZ
capabilities.doc: A body's world position along z.

capabilities.name: bodyVelX
capabilities.doc: A body's velocity along x, in metres per second.

capabilities.name: bodyVelY
capabilities.doc: A body's velocity along y, in metres per second.

capabilities.name: bodyVelZ
capabilities.doc: A body's velocity along z, in metres per second.

capabilities.name: bodyMass
capabilities.doc: A body's mass in kilograms, or zero where it has none because it is static or kinematic.

capabilities.name: sleeping
capabilities.doc: Whether a body has been still long enough to stop being solved.

capabilities.name: raycast
capabilities.signature: fn(world: PhysicsWorld, x: f32, y: f32, z: f32, dx: f32, dy: f32, dz: f32, maxDistance: f32, mask: i32) -> bool
capabilities.doc: Cast a ray and record what it hit. `mask` is required: without one the first thing a ray finds is often the body it started inside. Read the result with the `hit` functions.

capabilities.name: hitBody
capabilities.doc: The body the last `raycast` on this world found, or −1. Valid until the next raycast.

capabilities.name: hitX
capabilities.doc: Where the last raycast struck, along x. Valid until the next raycast.

capabilities.name: hitY
capabilities.doc: Where the last raycast struck, along y. Valid until the next raycast.

capabilities.name: hitZ
capabilities.doc: Where the last raycast struck, along z. Valid until the next raycast.

capabilities.name: hitNormalX
capabilities.doc: The surface normal the last raycast struck, along x.

capabilities.name: hitNormalY
capabilities.doc: The surface normal the last raycast struck, along y.

capabilities.name: hitNormalZ
capabilities.doc: The surface normal the last raycast struck, along z.

capabilities.name: hitFraction
capabilities.doc: How far along the ray the last hit was, from 0 to 1.

capabilities.name: contactCount
capabilities.doc: How many contact events the last step produced. Drain them after stepping, never during.

capabilities.name: contactKind
capabilities.doc: An event's kind: 0 entered, 1 still touching, 2 left.

capabilities.name: contactA
capabilities.doc: The lower-indexed body of a contact event.

capabilities.name: contactB
capabilities.doc: The higher-indexed body of a contact event.

capabilities.name: applyImpulse
capabilities.signature: fn(world: PhysicsWorld, body: i32, px: f32, py: f32, pz: f32, atX: f32, atY: f32, atZ: f32) -> void
capabilities.doc: Apply an impulse at a world point. The point is required: through the centre of mass an impulse produces no rotation at all, which reads as a broken impulse rather than a missing argument.

capabilities.name: applyForce
capabilities.signature: fn(world: PhysicsWorld, body: i32, fx: f32, fy: f32, fz: f32, dt: f32, atX: f32, atY: f32, atZ: f32) -> void
capabilities.doc: A force applied for one step, which is an impulse of force times dt. The point is required for the same reason.

capabilities.name: setVelocity
capabilities.signature: fn(world: PhysicsWorld, body: i32, vx: f32, vy: f32, vz: f32) -> void
capabilities.doc: Set a body's velocity outright, waking its island.

capabilities.name: setPosition
capabilities.signature: fn(world: PhysicsWorld, body: i32, x: f32, y: f32, z: f32) -> void
capabilities.doc: Move a body outright. A teleport rather than a push: the broadphase moves with it.

capabilities.name: wake
capabilities.doc: Wake a body and everything sharing its island, because a sleeping neighbour would settle it again.

capabilities.name: setGravity
capabilities.signature: fn(world: PhysicsWorld, x: f32, y: f32, z: f32) -> void
capabilities.doc: The world's gravity, in metres per second squared.

capabilities.name: spawn
capabilities.doc: Make one, with every component the prefab names. Overrides are the host’s to apply; a script that wants a different value writes it after.

capabilities.name: unit
capabilities.doc: A value from 0 to 1 for a seed. The same seed always gives the same value.

capabilities.name: range
capabilities.signature: fn(seed: u32, low: f32, high: f32) -> f32
capabilities.doc: A value between two bounds for a seed.

capabilities.name: index
capabilities.doc: An index into a collection of `count` items. Zero for an empty one.

capabilities.name: bloom
capabilities.doc: How much of the frame's bloom ceiling to take, 0 to 1. Held until changed. Does nothing when the quality profile's `bloom` is 0, because the chain is never built.

capabilities.name: exposure
capabilities.doc: How far this frame is scaled into the tone curve, above 0. Replaces the profile's `outputExposure` for this frame onward. Adaptation is yours: a game knows it walked into a cave, and the renderer could only find out a frame late. Ignored unless the output transform is `aces`, since otherwise there is no curve to be exposed into.

capabilities.name: motionBlur
capabilities.doc: How much of the camera motion blur ceiling this frame takes, 0 to 1. Held until changed. Ramp it with whatever "fast" means here: blur that is always on stops being a speed cue within seconds and costs eight taps a moving pixel while doing so.

capabilities.name: speedBlur
capabilities.doc: How much speed blur the frame resolves with, 0 to 1. Held until changed, and ignored when screen effects are off.

capabilities.name: focus
capabilities.signature: fn(renderer: Renderer, distance: f32, range: f32, scale: f32) -> void
capabilities.doc: Where this frame's lens is focused and how deep the sharp zone is, in metres, and how much of the depth-of-field ceiling to take, 0 to 1. Held until changed. `scale` is required here though the engine defaults it to 1, because taking the whole ceiling is the expensive answer and a script author is further from that cost than a TypeScript caller.

capabilities.name: medium
capabilities.signature: fn(renderer: Renderer, density: f32, albedo: f32, anisotropy: f32, maxDistance: f32) -> void
capabilities.doc: How thick the air is: a medium filling the whole frustum, rather than a beam inside a hull. `density` is extinction per metre and 0 is off — nothing is allocated and nothing is drawn, so a script that never raises it costs nothing. `albedo` is how much of what the air takes out comes back as light rather than heat, 0 to 1; `anisotropy` is -1 back to 1 forward, and is what makes haze glow toward a low sun; `maxDistance` is where the search for light to scatter stops, in metres, which is not where the fog stops. Held until changed. Does nothing when the quality profile's `globalMediumSteps` is 0, because no march is built.

capabilities.name: veil
capabilities.signature: fn(renderer: Renderer, red: f32, green: f32, blue: f32, alpha: f32) -> void
capabilities.doc: Composite a flat colour over the finished frame, for a cut dipping to white or to black. **Once per frame: a frame that does not call this draws with no veil at all**, unlike the dials above, because a transition that forgets to turn itself off is worse than one that forgets to turn on.

capabilities.name: presenting
capabilities.doc: Whether a session is running. False before one starts and after the user takes the headset off.

capabilities.name: supported
capabilities.doc: Whether this device could present at all. False on a machine with no headset attached.

capabilities.name: headX
capabilities.doc: Where the viewer’s head is, in metres. Zero outside a session.

capabilities.name: headY
capabilities.doc: Where the viewer’s head is, in metres. Zero outside a session.

capabilities.name: headZ
capabilities.doc: Where the viewer’s head is, in metres. Zero outside a session.

capabilities.name: trigger
capabilities.doc: How far a hand’s trigger is pulled, 0 to 1. Zero for a hand that is not there.

capabilities.name: squeeze
capabilities.doc: How far a hand’s grip is squeezed, 0 to 1. Zero for a hand that is not there.

capabilities.name: holding
capabilities.doc: Whether a hand is tracked this frame. False while a controller is set down or out of view.

capabilities.name: jointX
capabilities.doc: Where a named hand joint is, in metres. Zero for a joint that is not tracked.

capabilities.name: jointY
capabilities.doc: Where a named hand joint is, in metres. Zero for a joint that is not tracked.

capabilities.name: jointZ
capabilities.doc: Where a named hand joint is, in metres. Zero for a joint that is not tracked.

capabilities.name: pinching
capabilities.doc: Whether a hand’s thumb and index tips are close enough to count as a pinch.

capabilities.name: positionX
capabilities.doc: A node's local x.

capabilities.name: positionY
capabilities.doc: A node's local y.

capabilities.name: positionZ
capabilities.doc: A node's local z.

capabilities.name: setPosition
capabilities.signature: fn(node: Node, x: f32, y: f32, z: f32) -> void
capabilities.doc: Move a node, marking it and its subtree for a world update.

capabilities.name: setScale
capabilities.signature: fn(node: Node, x: f32, y: f32, z: f32) -> void
capabilities.doc: Scale a node.

capabilities.name: setRotation
capabilities.signature: fn(node: Node, x: f32, y: f32, z: f32, radians: f32) -> void
capabilities.doc: Rotate a node about an axis.

capabilities.name: windDirectionX
capabilities.doc: The prevailing wind's x, normalised; zero when there is no wind to have a direction.

capabilities.name: windDirectionZ
capabilities.doc: The prevailing wind's z, normalised; zero when there is no wind to have a direction.

capabilities.name: windSpeed
capabilities.doc: How hard it is blowing, metres a second, never negative.

capabilities.name: windGust
capabilities.doc: The gust alone, -1 to 1, for a behaviour that wants the deviation and not the total.

capabilities.name: distance
capabilities.doc: The distance between two nodes, in local space.

capabilities.name: sprite
capabilities.signature: fn(batch: SpriteBatch, texture: i32, x: f32, y: f32, w: f32, h: f32) -> void
capabilities.doc: Put one quad in the batch, covering the whole of a texture.

capabilities.name: tinted
capabilities.signature: fn(batch: SpriteBatch, texture: i32, x: f32, y: f32, w: f32, h: f32, r: f32, g: f32, b: f32, a: f32) -> void
capabilities.doc: The same, multiplied by a colour. White is the identity, so a white texture draws exactly this colour — which is how a solid rectangle is drawn.

capabilities.name: frame
capabilities.signature: fn(batch: SpriteBatch, sheet: SpriteSheet, frame: i32, x: f32, y: f32, w: f32, h: f32) -> void
capabilities.doc: Put one frame of a sheet in the batch. A frame the sheet does not have draws the whole sheet, which is unmistakable.

capabilities.name: named
capabilities.doc: The index a name has in a sheet, or -1. Ask once and keep the number: a name lookup is a hash and a frame is an array read.

capabilities.name: frames
capabilities.doc: How many frames the sheet was cut into.

capabilities.name: tilemap
capabilities.signature: fn(batch: SpriteBatch, map: Tilemap, sheet: SpriteSheet, x: f32, y: f32, w: f32, h: f32) -> i32
capabilities.doc: Draw the tiles a view rectangle can see, and answer how many that was. The cost is the view rather than the map.

capabilities.name: tile
capabilities.signature: fn(map: Tilemap, column: i32, row: i32) -> i32
capabilities.doc: The frame in a cell, or -1 for an empty one — including for a cell outside the map, which answers empty rather than another row.

capabilities.name: setTile
capabilities.signature: fn(map: Tilemap, column: i32, row: i32, tile: i32) -> void
capabilities.doc: Put a frame in a cell. A cell outside the map is ignored rather than wrapping into another row.

capabilities.name: columns
capabilities.doc: How wide the map is, in cells.

capabilities.name: rows
capabilities.doc: How tall the map is, in cells.

capabilities.name: count
capabilities.doc: How many quads are in the batch this frame.

capabilities.name: dropped
capabilities.doc: How many quads did not fit this frame. Zero is the only good value; anything else is a batch that wants a bigger capacity.

capabilities.name: layout
capabilities.signature: fn(tree: UiTree, x: f32, y: f32, w: f32, h: f32) -> void
capabilities.doc: Lay the tree out into a box. The box is what is available: a tree sized by its contents comes to what its contents come to.

capabilities.name: draw
capabilities.signature: fn(tree: UiTree, batch: SpriteBatch, white: i32) -> i32
capabilities.doc: Put the tree in a batch and answer how many quads that was. `white` is the sprite pass's own white slot, which is what a background is drawn on.

capabilities.name: has
capabilities.doc: Whether the tree holds a node of this name. Every reader below answers a defined value without it, so this is for a script that wants to know rather than one that would crash.

capabilities.name: left
capabilities.doc: Where a node ended up, along x. Zero for a name the tree does not hold.

capabilities.name: top
capabilities.doc: The same, along y.

capabilities.name: width
capabilities.doc: How wide a node ended up.

capabilities.name: height
capabilities.doc: How tall a node ended up.

capabilities.name: visible
capabilities.doc: Whether a node is shown. A hidden node is out of the layout and out of the hit test, not merely invisible.

capabilities.name: show
capabilities.signature: fn(tree: UiTree, name: String, visible: bool) -> void
capabilities.doc: Show or hide a node and everything under it.

capabilities.name: setText
capabilities.signature: fn(tree: UiTree, name: String, text: String) -> void
capabilities.doc: Change what a node says. What draws it is the caller's: this package draws quads, and core already draws two kinds of text.

capabilities.name: tint
capabilities.signature: fn(tree: UiTree, name: String, r: f32, g: f32, b: f32, a: f32) -> void
capabilities.doc: Change a node's background colour. A node with no background gets one.

capabilities.name: hovered
capabilities.doc: Whether the pointer is over a node.

capabilities.name: pressed
capabilities.doc: Whether the pointer went down on a node and has not come up.

capabilities.name: focused
capabilities.doc: Whether a node has the keyboard.

capabilities.name: point
capabilities.signature: fn(tree: UiTree, x: f32, y: f32, down: bool) -> bool
capabilities.doc: Route the pointer, and answer whether this call activated anything. An activation is a press and a release on the same node, so somebody who pressed the wrong button can slide off it.

capabilities.name: activated
capabilities.doc: Whether the last `point` activated this node. Read it in the same step that called `point`; the next one clears it.

capabilities.name: key
capabilities.signature: fn(tree: UiTree, key: String, shift: bool) -> bool
capabilities.doc: Route a key, and answer whether it activated what has focus. Tab moves focus, Enter and space activate, and everything else is reported unhandled so the caller can have it.

capabilities.name: focus
capabilities.doc: Give a node the keyboard. A name the tree does not hold focuses nothing.

capabilities.name: heightAt
capabilities.signature: fn(terrain: Terrain, x: float, z: float) -> float
capabilities.doc: How high the ground is at a place, in metres. The surface that is drawn, not an approximation of it, so a thing put here stands on what you can see.

capabilities.name: normalX
capabilities.signature: fn(terrain: Terrain, x: float, z: float) -> float
capabilities.doc: Which way the ground faces at a place, along x.

capabilities.name: normalY
capabilities.signature: fn(terrain: Terrain, x: float, z: float) -> float
capabilities.doc: The same, along y. One on the flat and smaller on a slope.

capabilities.name: normalZ
capabilities.signature: fn(terrain: Terrain, x: float, z: float) -> float
capabilities.doc: The same, along z.

capabilities.name: slopeAt
capabilities.signature: fn(terrain: Terrain, x: float, z: float) -> float
capabilities.doc: How steep the ground is at a place, in radians from flat. Zero on the level; a quarter turn on a wall.

capabilities.name: covers
capabilities.signature: fn(terrain: Terrain, x: float, z: float) -> bool
capabilities.doc: Whether a place is over the field at all. A query outside it answers the nearest edge rather than nothing, so ask this first where it matters.

capabilities.name: extentX
capabilities.doc: How far the field reaches along x, in metres.

capabilities.name: extentZ
capabilities.doc: How far the field reaches along z, in metres.

capabilities.name: fixedDelta
capabilities.doc: The fixed simulation step, in seconds. Prefer the `dt` your function was given.

capabilities.name: frameDelta
capabilities.doc: Seconds since the previous rendered frame, after clamping.

capabilities.name: wallDelta
capabilities.doc: Seconds of real time since the previous frame, unclamped. Outside the boundary in every sense.

capabilities.name: elapsed
capabilities.doc: Seconds since the loop started.

types.name: Agent
types.doc: A live agent session. Held and passed back; never read into.

types.name: Sound
types.doc: A decoded sound, resolved from a slot. Held and passed back; never read into.

types.name: Skeleton
types.doc: A joint hierarchy, parents before children.

types.name: Pose
types.doc: One set of joint transforms.

types.name: Clip
types.doc: Keyframed tracks over time.

types.name: Blend
types.doc: A blend tree over clips.

types.name: Motion
types.doc: A root's displacement over an interval.

types.name: Chemistry
types.doc: A chemistry world: parcels, the air, and the tick that runs them.

types.name: Substance
types.doc: A registered material: what it is made of and what it can turn into.

types.name: Species
types.doc: A registered chemical species, such as `O2` or `cellulose`.

types.name: Node
types.doc: A node in the transform hierarchy.

types.name: Wind
types.doc: The wind as it was sampled this frame.

types.name: Colliders
types.doc: A set of convex colliders with a spatial hash.

types.name: PhysicsWorld
types.doc: A rigid body world, stepped on the fixed clock.

types.name: Actions
types.doc: A bound action map: what the player is pressing.

types.name: Camera
types.doc: A cinematic camera.

types.name: Queue
types.doc: A priority message queue with dedupe and a ceiling.

types.name: Store
types.doc: A key-value store the consumer supplied.

types.name: World
types.doc: A world: its entities, their components and its systems.

types.name: Cursor
types.doc: A query in progress. Borrowed from the world's pool and given back when the walk ends, so it may not outlive the loop that opened it.

types.name: View
types.doc: A component's live columns. The object stays valid across a reallocation; the arrays inside it do not, so index through the view rather than holding one.

types.name: Behavior
types.doc: One agent running one behaviour tree: where it is in its routine.

types.name: NavGraph
types.doc: A network of places and the ways between them.

types.name: NavPath
types.doc: A route being walked, and how far along it the walker is. Ask it where to steer.

types.name: Terrain
types.doc: A heightfield: ask it how high the ground is and which way it faces.

types.name: SpriteBatch
types.doc: One frame of quads, in the order they were put in. Reset it, fill it, draw it.

types.name: SpriteSheet
types.doc: The rectangles of one texture that each hold a picture, addressed by index or by name.

types.name: Tilemap
types.doc: A grid of sheet frames. Drawing one costs the view rather than the map.

types.name: UiTree
types.doc: The root of a retained interface tree. Its nodes are addressed by the names they were built with.

types.name: Gizmo
types.doc: A transform tool: what the pointer is over, and the transform a drag is editing.

types.name: Editor
types.doc: An editing session: what is selected, the tree of what exists, and whether the world is playing.

types.name: Session
types.doc: A networking session: who this peer is, what it can see of the others, and the scalars it publishes.

types.name: Rewind
types.doc: The rewind loop: which tick is running, whether this is a replay, and how far back it can reach.

types.name: Renderer
types.doc: The renderer drawing this frame. Reaches a script through `uses`.
